name: Jenkins
tagline: Automates build, test and release pipelines defined as code in Git.

howItWorks.title: What it is and where it sits
howItWorks.body:
Jenkins is a Java automation server that runs pipelines on triggers.
It works at L7: HTTP for UI and webhooks, SSH or WebSocket to agents.
The controller schedules and stores; agents execute the work.
It sits between source control and the registry or cluster it releases to.
It does not store artifacts; it hands them to a registry.

howItWorks.title: Controller and agents
howItWorks.body:
The controller holds config, credentials, job history and the build queue.
Set controller executors to 0; agents run every build.
Agents join by SSH, inbound WebSocket, or as short-lived Docker and Kubernetes pods.
Labels route a stage to the right agent, such as docker or arm64.
JENKINS_HOME is the state to persist and back up.

howItWorks.title: Declarative pipeline
howItWorks.body:
A Jenkinsfile in Git defines agent, environment, options, stages and post.
The parser validates structure before the first step runs.
when conditions restrict deploy stages to the main branch.
parallel stages shorten feedback; post blocks handle cleanup and notifications.
Put reusable logic in shared libraries, not copied Groovy.

howItWorks.title: Triggers and source control
howItWorks.body:
A webhook from the Git host starts a build immediately; polling is the fallback.
Multibranch pipelines create a job per branch and pull request automatically.
Branch discovery reads the Jenkinsfile found in each branch.
Use a read-only deploy key or token for checkout.
Skip builds for docs-only changes with when and changeset conditions.

howItWorks.title: Credentials and security
howItWorks.body:
The Credentials plugin stores secrets encrypted under JENKINS_HOME/secrets.
Bind them with credentials() or withCredentials; logs mask the values.
Scope credentials to a folder and grant least privilege.
Use role-based or matrix authorisation; disable anonymous access.
Put TLS on a reverse proxy and keep the agent port closed to the world.

howItWorks.title: Typical delivery stages
howItWorks.body:
Checkout, build, unit test, static analysis, quality gate, image build, scan, push.
Cheap checks run first; any failed gate stops the pipeline.
Tag images with the commit SHA, never only latest.
Archive test reports with junit so trends show in the UI.
Keep the pipeline short; slow end-to-end suites run on a schedule.

howItWorks.title: HA, observability and failure modes
howItWorks.body:
Open-source Jenkins runs one active controller; recover by restoring JENKINS_HOME to a new node.
Configure it as code with JCasC and pin plugin versions.
The Prometheus plugin exposes queue length, executor use and job durations.
Common failures: offline agents, full disks, plugin upgrade breakage, expired credentials.
Read the build console first, then the controller log under /var/log/jenkins.

howItWorks.title: What sits in front
howItWorks.body:
A push to Git fires a webhook, or a poll or schedule trigger, at the controller.
Users reach the controller UI through a reverse proxy at the Edge.
The Jenkinsfile lives in the repository, versioned with the code.
The controller holds credentials, queue and history; it runs no builds.

howItWorks.title: What sits behind
howItWorks.body:
Agents are Linux VMs joined over SSH, or pods started by the Kubernetes plugin.
Stages call SonarQube, Trivy, a registry and a cluster.
Deploy by kubectl or helm from a stage, or commit an image tag to a config repo for a GitOps tool.
Argo CD or Flux then reconciles the cluster from Git.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
GitLab CI: choose it when code, issues and CI should live in one product.
GitHub Actions: choose it for hosted runners and a repository-native workflow.
Tekton: Kubernetes-native pipelines defined as cluster resources.
Argo Workflows or CircleCI: pick them for in-cluster DAGs or a hosted service.

flow: A developer pushes to Git; a webhook reaches the controller.
The controller reads the Jenkinsfile and queues the build.
An agent, either a VM or a pod, checks out, builds and tests.
Static analysis and the quality gate must pass.
The image is scanned, then pushed with an immutable tag.
The pipeline commits the new tag to the config repo.
Argo CD syncs the cluster to match Git.
Alternatively, a stage runs kubectl or helm directly.
A smoke test checks the live endpoint.

deploy.summary: Jenkins LTS on a Linux VM under systemd, hardened SSH, one SSH agent, then pipelines.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 VM, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM
Sudo access and a static IP

steps.title: SSH keys and sshd hardening
steps.code:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -C ops@example.com
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ops@192.0.2.10
sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-hardening.conf <<'EOF'
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
EOF
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
steps.note: 192.0.2.10 is a placeholder. Keep a second session open until key login works.

steps.title: Static address and DNS
steps.code:
# /etc/netplan/60-static.yaml (placeholders)
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    ens18:
      addresses: [192.0.2.10/24]
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 192.0.2.1
      nameservers:
        addresses: [192.0.2.2]
# then: sudo netplan apply
# DNS: ci.example.com. IN A 192.0.2.10
steps.note: Match the interface name from ip -br link. Use your own subnet.

steps.title: Install Java and Jenkins LTS
steps.code:
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y fontconfig openjdk-17-jre curl
sudo wget -O /usr/share/keyrings/jenkins-keyring.asc https://pkg.jenkins.io/debian-stable/jenkins.io-2023.key
echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/jenkins-keyring.asc] https://pkg.jenkins.io/debian-stable binary/' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/jenkins.list
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jenkins
apt-cache policy jenkins | head -3
steps.note: Pin with apt-mark hold jenkins after choosing an LTS version.

steps.title: systemd service and firewall
steps.code:
sudo systemctl enable --now jenkins
sudo systemctl status jenkins --no-pager
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp
sudo ufw enable
sudo cat /var/lib/jenkins/secrets/initialAdminPassword
steps.note: Put NGINX with TLS in front, then close 8080 to everyone but the proxy.

steps.title: Agent VM over SSH
steps.code:
# on the agent VM
sudo apt-get install -y openjdk-17-jre git docker.io
sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash jenkins-agent && sudo mkdir -p /home/jenkins-agent/.ssh
# on the controller: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/agent_key -N ''
# paste agent_key.pub into /home/jenkins-agent/.ssh/authorized_keys
# UI: Manage Jenkins > Nodes > New Node > Launch via SSH, credential agent-ssh
# UI: Built-In Node > Number of executors = 0
steps.note: Add the agent to the docker group only if builds need it.

steps.title: Pipeline: build, scan, push, GitOps
steps.note: Save as Jenkinsfile. Registry, repo URLs and make targets are placeholders. Argo CD then syncs the config repo.

steps.title: Kubernetes pod agent and direct deploy
steps.note: Needs the Kubernetes and Kubernetes CLI plugins plus a cloud entry. Prefer the GitOps hand-off for production.

steps.title: Hand off to Argo CD
steps.code:
# token created in Argo CD for a CI account, stored as Jenkins secret text
export ARGOCD_SERVER=argocd.example.com   # placeholder
export ARGOCD_AUTH_TOKEN="$ARGOCD_TOKEN"
argocd app sync app --grpc-web
argocd app wait app --health --timeout 300
steps.note: Optional: with auto-sync on, Argo CD picks up the Git commit by itself.

verify: Agent online: Manage Jenkins > Nodes shows the agent without a red cross
Deployed: kubectl -n dev rollout status deployment/app
pitfalls: Builds on the controller expose credentials; keep executors at 0.
Unpinned plugins break upgrades; pin versions and test updates on a copy.
Mounting the Docker socket gives builds root on the host.
Hardcoded secrets in a Jenkinsfile leak through Git history; use credentials().
Without a JENKINS_HOME backup, a lost controller loses jobs and secrets.
A cluster-admin kubeconfig in Jenkins is a blast-radius risk; scope it to a namespace.
Stale workspaces fill the disk; use cleanWs() and buildDiscarder.
keyPoints: The controller schedules and records; agents run the builds.
A declarative Jenkinsfile in Git defines every stage and gate.
Credentials are injected at runtime and masked in logs.
Deploy by direct kubectl or by committing a tag for Argo CD.
quickDeploy: Install Java 17 and the Jenkins LTS package.
Start the systemd service and unlock the UI.
Attach an SSH agent and set controller executors to 0.
Commit a Jenkinsfile and run the pipeline.
osiNote: Orchestrates over HTTP, SSH and webhooks; builds run on agents.
production: Run the controller with zero executors; build only on agents.
Back up JENKINS_HOME nightly and test the restore.
Define the controller in JCasC and pin plugin versions.
Role-based access, no anonymous read, TLS on a reverse proxy.
Scrape the Prometheus plugin; alert on queue length and agent offline.
